column1: # Accepted CodeQL findings. The gate in pr-checks.yml ignores exactly
# these, and nothing else. Changing this file takes a pull request.

column3: ONVIF WS-UsernameToken PasswordDigest is defined by the standard as base64(sha1(nonce + created + password)); the camera requires it this way. The proxy computes it to sign in to the camera, and never stores passwords hashed with it.

Baichuan, the camera's own protocol, derives its AES session key from md5(nonce-password) and the login from md5 hashes of user and password; the camera requires it (reolink_aio, measured on the RLC-1224A). The proxy computes it only to sign in to the camera and never stores passwords hashed with it.

The one-off camera probe (docs/multi-camera-host.md §12) reads the certificate a camera serves, to record it before the site CA exists: the camera's factory certificate is self-signed, so it is read without validation. Nothing is sent on that connection (it is closed after the handshake); the camera API calls go through ReolinkClient as everywhere else. Not used by the proxy.

servedCertificate() reads the certificate a camera serves (its factory certificate is self-signed, or a site-CA leaf) to compare its SHA-256 with the leaf the proxy pushed: a push is judged only by that fingerprint (spec 2026-10-05-multi-camera-host-design §10.1.3). Nothing is sent on that connection (closed right after the handshake). Every camera API call, the push's included, goes through ReolinkClient, verified against the site CA or pinned (SHA-256, in the handshake) to the certificate read here just before.
